tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Contributing

This repository is a clean-room, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE
FM-1 pocket synthesizer (JieLi AC791N). The FM-1's existing community
firmwares are GPL-licensed; ours must be provably independent of them. The
rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
owner** before you open it.

## Roles

Clean-room work separates the people who have seen the protected code from
the people who write ours.

- **Spec side (exposed).** May read the F-Emulator emulator's source, whose
  chip model was partly written from the hardware layer (`hal/`) of the
  Felucca firmware, hugelton/Felucca, licensed GPL-3.0 (docs/EXPOSURE.md,
  "Corrections", 2026-10-23). Builds the test harness and writes
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only (addresses, bits, pins, timings,
  protocols), never code or code structure, each fact citing a non-GPL
  source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, results of its own black-box
  experiments, and a porter's reports in `ports/`. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.

- **Auditor (exposed to the GPL firmwares).** A third role, only for a
  failed similarity audit (docs/AUDIT.md, "When the audit fails"). The owner
  starts one; it works in a folder of its own set up with
  `tools/auditor-setup.sh` (settings `config/claude/auditor.json`), and may
  read the flagged GPL target files and our code. It writes only a finding
  in `audit/findings/`, in general terms (which of our files, the scores,
  the conclusion; never target code). It never writes firmware, the spec or
  the harness, then or in any later session. Its transcript holds GPL
  source, so it is **never archived in this repository**: it goes to the
  owner's private repository `small-beeps-audit` (created, with the
  owner's approval, when the first auditor session runs), committed there
  with an OpenTimestamps proof, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records the session's
  ID, the transcript's SHA-256 and that repository's commit.

- **Porter (exposed to the GPL firmwares).** A fourth role, since session
  day-1024. It may read GPL FM-1 engines (the firmwares and engines on
  the list below) to port them onto our base, and does that work in a
  separate repository, `small-beeps-ports`, under the GPL (created with
  the owner's approval when the first porter session runs). The owner
  starts one; it works in a folder of its own set up with
  `tools/porter-setup.sh` (settings `config/claude/porter.json`), a full
  clone of this repository that it reads, with the port repository cloned
  inside it as `port-work/` (gitignored here), where all its GPL work
  goes. In this repository it writes only two things: its entry in
  docs/EXPOSURE.md, and reports in `ports/` (`ports/README.md`): what a
  port measured on our base (cycles, memory, voices, timings) and what it
  needs from the base (API requests), in general terms, never code, code
  structure or names from a GPL engine. It never writes into `firmware/`,
  the spec, the harness or anything else here, then or in any later
  session, and never becomes spec side or firmware side. Its transcripts
  hold GPL source, so they are **never archived in this repository**:
  they go to the port repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records each
  session's ID, its transcript's SHA-256 and that repository's commit.
  The firmware side reads a report as it reads a spec request's answer:
  through the facts in it, logged in PROVENANCE.md, and answers an API
  request with its own design.

Every person and every session is recorded in docs/EXPOSURE.md with its role
and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in
EXPOSURE.md at once, and stop writing firmware.

## Clean-room rules

### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes

- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
- any other FM-1 firmware source;
- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com;
- the port repository `small-beeps-ports` and a porter's `port-work/`
  folder (the porter's GPL ports; since day-1024).
- FM-1-RE's `docs/io/09-storage.md` (since evening-1024, the owner's
  decision): most of it describes the stock firmware's own code (its
  routines and its own record and patch storage). The spec side may still
  read it and cites only its hardware facts in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, which is
  how those facts reach the firmware side. `tools/check-transcripts.py`
  applies this entry to sessions from 2026-10-25 on (M7 read the document
  while it was allowed; docs/EXPOSURE.md).

`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together). Since
M4 it fails a call that accesses listed material (reads, lists, searches,
fetches or checks it out) and logs, report only, one that only mentions it
(sessions/README.md).

### Firmware side may use

Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:

- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
  source);
- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
  update-protocol documents only, except `docs/io/09-storage.md` (see the
  list above). Fetch single documents by URL; never clone it (a clone puts
  its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
- public datasheets;
- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`;
- a porter's reports in `ports/` (measurements and API requests, in
  general terms; CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles").

### Barriers

- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
- **Records in a clean folder.** Each record on the `records` branch also
  keeps the harness's own test results and the hashes of their outputs.
  Records before SR-1-SR-2 also keep the spec experiments' outputs (memory
  dumps, captures, audio); since then a record keeps only their names and
  SHA-256 (`spec-experiments.sha256`), and older records stay as they are.
  Clean sessions never fetch the records branch wholesale (no `git archive`, checkout or
  lazy fetch of a whole record or of the branch): they fetch only named
  files of the firmware's own records, `report.json`, `report.md` and
  named logs under `logs/`, one path at a time. `tools/clean-update.sh`
  also stops if a file under a `harness/` or `spec-experiments/` folder,
  or under the excluded folders, is in `.git` through any branch, the
  records branch included (since M1, after a wholesale fetch brought 17
  such outputs into a clean folder; docs/EXPOSURE.md).
  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
  `config/claude/spec.json`.
- **One list of the spec-side folders.** `config/spec-side-folders` names
  the three folders once (since M3). The barrier tools build every name,
  pattern and exclusion from it, and their tests use made-up names
  (`tests/helpers.py`), so changing them needs no command that names the
  folders. Scratch test repositories made by hand use the made-up names
  too. The deny lists keep their literal paths (Claude Code's syntax), and
  C-UNIT checks they cover every folder on the list and that no barrier
  tool or test spells one out.
- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
  non-zero if they differ.
- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
  of every session, before anything else:
  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.
Since M4b the terms of the vendored Plaits (`vendor/plaits/`, read only from
its checksum-verified files) are public like the SDK's, the check says how
many emulator terms that takes off, and `vendor/plaits/` itself is not
scanned, except its `SOURCE.md`, which we write (R-SEP-1).

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

```
<area>: <what changed, one line>

What:    what this commit does
Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
```

- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
  the agent; the owner is the committer.
- Small commits: one idea each.
- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
  carries the sections.

`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).

## Pull requests and merging

- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
  links to the CI run and the record).
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main, and the similarity
  audit's report beside it (`records/<sha>/audit/`) only by
  `.github/workflows/audit.yml`'s record job (docs/AUDIT.md). Both use the
  `records` environment's deploy key.
- **Performance budgets** (`config/budgets.json`, R-PERF-1) are raised, or
  moved to the next milestone's, only by a pull request of their own that
  says why in the What/Why/How/Result sections and changes nothing else.
  When CI's performance summary shows an improvement of more than 3%
  (R-PERF-2), say so in the pull request's Result.
- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key
  (below), and a GitHub release with the build outputs, the record and an
  SBOM.

### Merge policy and its history

- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs
  with GitHub's key instead.
- **2026-10-22:** pull request #1 was merged with the button. Its merge
  commit `2fd28219` is signed by GitHub (`web-flow`, verified), and its
  record shows C-MERGE **FAIL** under the old rule ("committer is web-flow,
  not the owner"). The record stays as it is, and history is not rewritten.
- **2026-10-22:** the owner then chose button merges for good. The bypass
  was removed from the main ruleset, so the rules now apply to everyone.

What a merge on main proves: GitHub's signature shows the commit was made
by GitHub on the owner's merge. `merged_by` shows the owner pressed the
button. The required `ci` check shows CI passed on exactly the merged head.
The records workflow re-checks all of this for every push to main
(C-MERGE): a merge commit, a verified signature, committer `web-flow` with
the pull request's `merged_by` the owner (or, for older merges, the owner
as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
is still written.

## Rulesets

Repository rulesets (Settings → Rules → Rulesets):

- **main**: restrict deletions; block force pushes; require a pull request
  before merging (allowed merge method: merge only); require status checks to
  pass (the `ci` job); no bypass (until 2026-10-22: the repository admin
  role).
- **records-history** (branch `records`): restrict deletions; block force
  pushes; no bypass.
- **records-writer** (branch `records`): restrict creations; restrict
  updates; bypass list: deploy keys only. Together these make the records
  workflow's deploy key the only writer, and it can only add commits.
- **milestone-tags** (tags `m*`): restrict deletions; restrict updates; no
  bypass.

Repository settings: allow merge commits only (squash and rebase merging
off).

Set up on 2026-10-22 by session M0a, with the owner's approval, through the
GitHub API:

| What | ID or fingerprint |
|------|-------------------|
| Ruleset `main` | 25612787 (required check `ci` from GitHub Actions; no bypass since 2026-10-22, before that the repository admin role) |
| Ruleset `records-history` | 25612788 |
| Ruleset `records-writer` | 25612790 (bypass: deploy keys) |
| Ruleset `milestone-tags` | 25612791 |
| Environment `records` | deployments from `main` only; secret `RECORDS_DEPLOY_KEY` |
| Deploy key "records workflow (records branch writer)" | 167260041, write access, ED25519 `SHA256:Od9RfSkzLwqLYSZRf1X7jEdcLhty0n1ISgQ+ec43Dkk` |

The deploy key's private half was generated in the session's scratch
folder, piped into the environment secret without being printed, and
deleted. To rotate it: make a new pair, replace the secret, add the new
public key, delete the old key.

## SSH signing for milestone tags (one-time setup, owner)

1. Create a signing key (or reuse an SSH key you already have):
   `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "small-beeps signing" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing`
2. Tell git to sign with it:
   ```sh
   git config --global gpg.format ssh
   git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing.pub
   git config --global tag.gpgSign true
   ```
   Leave `commit.gpgSign` off: merges are signed by GitHub's button.
3. Let git verify signatures locally: add a line
   `<your git email> <contents of id_ed25519_signing.pub>` to
   `~/.ssh/allowed_signers`, then
   `git config --global gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile ~/.ssh/allowed_signers`.
4. On GitHub: Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key → Key type
   **Signing Key**, and paste the `.pub` contents.
5. Tag a milestone: `git tag -s mN -m "mN"`, then `git push origin mN`.
6. Check: `git tag -v mN` shows "Good "git" signature", and GitHub shows the
   tag as **Verified**.

## Licences

- Every file we write starts with an SPDX header:
  `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` and `SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98`.
  Files that can't carry one are covered in `REUSE.toml`.
- Vendored files keep their own licences (`vendor/*/LICENSE`, `NOTICE`).
- CI runs `reuse lint` and fails on any gap (C-REUSE).
- Never commit the toolchain or anything containing it (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md).
- Nothing secret ever goes in: no keys, tokens or private notes. The
  repository is public and history is never rewritten.

## Privacy

The repository is public. No committed file, commit message or pull request
text names the owner's username, real name, e-mail address, hostname or
local folder names, or a full local path: write paths relative to the
repository, or as `~/...` with the top folder shown as `<top>`. Anyone who
finds such a term in the repository tells the owner instead of repeating it.

- **The terms** are kept by the owner, never in the repository: in the
  gitignored `tools/[REDACTED:host]` (one per line, `#` comments,
  matched ignoring case) and in the repository secret `PRIVATE_TERMS`, which
  CI passes to the check.
- **The check** `tools/check-private.py` (C-PRIVATE, R-PUB-3) scans every
  tracked file and every commit message, and the pre-commit and commit-msg
  hooks scan staged files and the message (`tools/install-hooks.sh` turns
  them on). A hit is reported by file and line only, never the term. CI
  fails when the secret is missing.
- **Records are scanned too** (since M1). Before a test record, an audit
  report or a C-MERGE re-check is hashed, uploaded or pushed, any file in
  it holding a term is withheld: deleted, and listed with the SHA-256 of
  the original in `WITHHELD.json`, which the record keeps (C-RECORD-PRIVATE).
  The original is not kept anywhere; the checks are deterministic, so it
  can be regenerated and matched to its hash. CI artifacts are kept 14 days.
- **Older records stay as they are.** A file under `sessions/` or
  `docs/prompts/` whose blob is identical to the same path at the base
  commit in `config/private-base` (the last main commit before the check)
  is exempt. This is decided from git's object hashes alone, so no session
  opens or lists the spec side's transcripts for it, and the check prints
  only how many files it exempted per folder. Every file added or changed
  after the base is checked in full. Files that sessions keep editing get no
  exemption: their current text is redacted instead (`docs/EXPOSURE.md` was,
  on 2026-10-22), and git history keeps the originals.
- **Archived transcripts** are redacted by `tools/archive-session.py`: the
  username anywhere it appears, the local top-level folder as `<top>`, and
  every private term.

## Low profile (for now)

The repository is public but unpromoted. In its name, description and topics,
and in README.md, never use these quiet words: **FM-1, M-VAVE, JieLi, synth,
firmware** (any spelling or case; `tools/check-low-profile.py` has the
patterns). Don't link the repository from anywhere, star it, fork it or
announce it. Everything else in the repository stays complete and truthful.
docs/GOING-PUBLIC.md says how this ends.

## Clean-room rules

### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes

- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
- any other FM-1 firmware source;
- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com;
- the port repository `small-beeps-ports` and a porter's `port-work/`
  folder (the porter's GPL ports; since day-1024).
- FM-1-RE's `docs/io/09-storage.md` (since evening-1024, the owner's
  decision): most of it describes the stock firmware's own code (its
  routines and its own record and patch storage). The spec side may still
  read it and cites only its hardware facts in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, which is
  how those facts reach the firmware side. `tools/check-transcripts.py`
  applies this entry to sessions from 2026-10-25 on (M7 read the document
  while it was allowed; docs/EXPOSURE.md).

`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together). Since
M4 it fails a call that accesses listed material (reads, lists, searches,
fetches or checks it out) and logs, report only, one that only mentions it
(sessions/README.md).

### Firmware side may use

Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:

- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
  source);
- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
  update-protocol documents only, except `docs/io/09-storage.md` (see the
  list above). Fetch single documents by URL; never clone it (a clone puts
  its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
- public datasheets;
- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`;
- a porter's reports in `ports/` (measurements and API requests, in
  general terms; CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles").

### Barriers

- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
- **Records in a clean folder.** Each record on the `records` branch also
  keeps the harness's own test results and the hashes of their outputs.
  Records before SR-1-SR-2 also keep the spec experiments' outputs (memory
  dumps, captures, audio); since then a record keeps only their names and
  SHA-256 (`spec-experiments.sha256`), and older records stay as they are.
  Clean sessions never fetch the records branch wholesale (no `git archive`, checkout or
  lazy fetch of a whole record or of the branch): they fetch only named
  files of the firmware's own records, `report.json`, `report.md` and
  named logs under `logs/`, one path at a time. `tools/clean-update.sh`
  also stops if a file under a `harness/` or `spec-experiments/` folder,
  or under the excluded folders, is in `.git` through any branch, the
  records branch included (since M1, after a wholesale fetch brought 17
  such outputs into a clean folder; docs/EXPOSURE.md).
  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
  `config/claude/spec.json`.
- **One list of the spec-side folders.** `config/spec-side-folders` names
  the three folders once (since M3). The barrier tools build every name,
  pattern and exclusion from it, and their tests use made-up names
  (`tests/helpers.py`), so changing them needs no command that names the
  folders. Scratch test repositories made by hand use the made-up names
  too. The deny lists keep their literal paths (Claude Code's syntax), and
  C-UNIT checks they cover every folder on the list and that no barrier
  tool or test spells one out.
- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
  non-zero if they differ.
- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
  of every session, before anything else:
  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.
Since M4b the terms of the vendored Plaits (`vendor/plaits/`, read only from
its checksum-verified files) are public like the SDK's, the check says how
many emulator terms that takes off, and `vendor/plaits/` itself is not
scanned, except its `SOURCE.md`, which we write (R-SEP-1).

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

```
<area>: <what changed, one line>

What:    what this commit does
Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
```

- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
  the agent; the owner is the committer.
- Small commits: one idea each.
- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
  carries the sections.

`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).

## Pull requests and merging

- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
  links to the CI run and the record).
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main, and the similarity
  audit's report beside it (`records/<sha>/audit/`) only by
  `.github/workflows/audit.yml`'s record job (docs/AUDIT.md). Both use the
  `records` environment's deploy key.
- **Performance budgets** (`config/budgets.json`, R-PERF-1) are raised, or
  moved to the next milestone's, only by a pull request of their own that
  says why in the What/Why/How/Result sections and changes nothing else.
  When CI's performance summary shows an improvement of more than 3%
  (R-PERF-2), say so in the pull request's Result.
- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key
  (below), and a GitHub release with the build outputs, the record and an
  SBOM.

### Merge policy and its history

- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs
  with GitHub's key instead.
- **2026-10-22:** pull request #1 was merged with the button. Its merge
  commit `2fd28219` is signed by GitHub (`web-flow`, verified), and its
  record shows C-MERGE **FAIL** under the old rule ("committer is web-flow,
  not the owner"). The record stays as it is, and history is not rewritten.
- **2026-10-22:** the owner then chose button merges for good. The bypass
  was removed from the main ruleset, so the rules now apply to everyone.

What a merge on main proves: GitHub's signature shows the commit was made
by GitHub on the owner's merge. `merged_by` shows the owner pressed the
button. The required `ci` check shows CI passed on exactly the merged head.
The records workflow re-checks all of this for every push to main
(C-MERGE): a merge commit, a verified signature, committer `web-flow` with
the pull request's `merged_by` the owner (or, for older merges, the owner
as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
is still written.

## Rulesets

Repository rulesets (Settings → Rules → Rulesets):

- **main**: restrict deletions; block force pushes; require a pull request
  before merging (allowed merge method: merge only); require status checks to
  pass (the `ci` job); no bypass (until 2026-10-22: the repository admin
  role).
- **records-history** (branch `records`): restrict deletions; block force
  pushes; no bypass.
- **records-writer** (branch `records`): restrict creations; restrict
  updates; bypass list: deploy keys only. Together these make the records
  workflow's deploy key the only writer, and it can only add commits.
- **milestone-tags** (tags `m*`): restrict deletions; restrict updates; no
  bypass.

Repository settings: allow merge commits only (squash and rebase merging
off).

Set up on 2026-10-22 by session M0a, with the owner's approval, through the
GitHub API:

| What | ID or fingerprint |
|------|-------------------|
| Ruleset `main` | 25612787 (required check `ci` from GitHub Actions; no bypass since 2026-10-22, before that the repository admin role) |
| Ruleset `records-history` | 25612788 |
| Ruleset `records-writer` | 25612790 (bypass: deploy keys) |
| Ruleset `milestone-tags` | 25612791 |
| Environment `records` | deployments from `main` only; secret `RECORDS_DEPLOY_KEY` |
| Deploy key "records workflow (records branch writer)" | 167260041, write access, ED25519 `SHA256:Od9RfSkzLwqLYSZRf1X7jEdcLhty0n1ISgQ+ec43Dkk` |

The deploy key's private half was generated in the session's scratch
folder, piped into the environment secret without being printed, and
deleted. To rotate it: make a new pair, replace the secret, add the new
public key, delete the old key.

## SSH signing for milestone tags (one-time setup, owner)

1. Create a signing key (or reuse an SSH key you already have):
   `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "small-beeps signing" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing`
2. Tell git to sign with it:
   ```sh
   git config --global gpg.format ssh
   git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing.pub
   git config --global tag.gpgSign true
   ```
   Leave `commit.gpgSign` off: merges are signed by GitHub's button.
3. Let git verify signatures locally: add a line
   `<your git email> <contents of id_ed25519_signing.pub>` to
   `~/.ssh/allowed_signers`, then
   `git config --global gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile ~/.ssh/allowed_signers`.
4. On GitHub: Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key → Key type
   **Signing Key**, and paste the `.pub` contents.
5. Tag a milestone: `git tag -s mN -m "mN"`, then `git push origin mN`.
6. Check: `git tag -v mN` shows "Good "git" signature", and GitHub shows the
   tag as **Verified**.

## Licences

- Every file we write starts with an SPDX header:
  `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` and `SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98`.
  Files that can't carry one are covered in `REUSE.toml`.
- Vendored files keep their own licences (`vendor/*/LICENSE`, `NOTICE`).
- CI runs `reuse lint` and fails on any gap (C-REUSE).
- Never commit the toolchain or anything containing it (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md).
- Nothing secret ever goes in: no keys, tokens or private notes. The
  repository is public and history is never rewritten.

## Privacy

The repository is public. No committed file, commit message or pull request
text names the owner's username, real name, e-mail address, hostname or
local folder names, or a full local path: write paths relative to the
repository, or as `~/...` with the top folder shown as `<top>`. Anyone who
finds such a term in the repository tells the owner instead of repeating it.

- **The terms** are kept by the owner, never in the repository: in the
  gitignored `tools/[REDACTED:host]` (one per line, `#` comments,
  matched ignoring case) and in the repository secret `PRIVATE_TERMS`, which
  CI passes to the check.
- **The check** `tools/check-private.py` (C-PRIVATE, R-PUB-3) scans every
  tracked file and every commit message, and the pre-commit and commit-msg
  hooks scan staged files and the message (`tools/install-hooks.sh` turns
  them on). A hit is reported by file and line only, never the term. CI
  fails when the secret is missing.
- **Records are scanned too** (since M1). Before a test record, an audit
  report or a C-MERGE re-check is hashed, uploaded or pushed, any file in
  it holding a term is withheld: deleted, and listed with the SHA-256 of
  the original in `WITHHELD.json`, which the record keeps (C-RECORD-PRIVATE).
  The original is not kept anywhere; the checks are deterministic, so it
  can be regenerated and matched to its hash. CI artifacts are kept 14 days.
- **Older records stay as they are.** A file under `sessions/` or
  `docs/prompts/` whose blob is identical to the same path at the base
  commit in `config/private-base` (the last main commit before the check)
  is exempt. This is decided from git's object hashes alone, so no session
  opens or lists the spec side's transcripts for it, and the check prints
  only how many files it exempted per folder. Every file added or changed
  after the base is checked in full. Files that sessions keep editing get no
  exemption: their current text is redacted instead (`docs/EXPOSURE.md` was,
  on 2026-10-22), and git history keeps the originals.
- **Archived transcripts** are redacted by `tools/archive-session.py`: the
  username anywhere it appears, the local top-level folder as `<top>`, and
  every private term.

## Low profile (for now)

The repository is public but unpromoted. In its name, description and topics,
and in README.md, never use these quiet words: **FM-1, M-VAVE, JieLi, synth,
firmware** (any spelling or case; `tools/check-low-profile.py` has the
patterns). Don't link the repository from anywhere, star it, fork it or
announce it. Everything else in the repository stays complete and truthful.
docs/GOING-PUBLIC.md says how this ends.

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Updates a clean folder to its remote's main (or REF), the safe way.
#
#   tools/clean-update.sh [--dir DIR] [REF]      (default: this folder, main)
#
# Clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, set
# by config/claude/clean.json), so no command can download a file the clean
# folder leaves out. A checkout of new commits needs lazy fetching for the
# files it does check out, so this script allows it for exactly one
# fast-forward, then re-applies the sparse checkout and checks that no file
# under a spec-side folder (config/spec-side-folders) reached the disk or the
# folder's .git, nor any spec-side file under another branch (the records
# branch keeps spec-side outputs). Stop and tell the owner if it fails.
#
# The fast-forward runs with --no-stat and -q: a merge summary (diffstat)
# counts the lines of every changed file, and with lazy fetching allowed git
# downloads the excluded files' contents to count them.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
if [ "${1:-}" = "--dir" ]; then ROOT=$(cd "$2" && pwd); shift 2; fi
ref=${1:-main}
role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
[ "$role" = clean ] || { echo "clean-update.sh is for clean folders (role here: ${role:-none})" >&2; exit 2; }

GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin
env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$ROOT" merge -q --no-stat --ff-only "origin/$ref"
GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" > /dev/null

# The spec-side folders, from the one list (since M3).
SPEC_FOLDERS=$(grep -v '^#' "$ROOT/config/spec-side-folders" | cut -f1)
[ -n "$SPEC_FOLDERS" ] || { echo "STOP: no spec-side folders in config/spec-side-folders"; exit 1; }
# Any path with one of them, or a spec-experiments/ folder, in it.
SPEC_RE="(^|/)(spec-experiments|$(printf '%s\n' "$SPEC_FOLDERS" | paste -sd '|' -))/"
fail=0
for p in $SPEC_FOLDERS; do
    [ ! -e "$ROOT/$p" ] || { echo "STOP: $p is on disk"; fail=1; }
    have=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' \
        | GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname)' 2>/dev/null | grep -vc missing || true)
    [ "$have" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: $have file(s) under $p are in .git"; fail=1; }
done
# Spec-side outputs can reach .git another way: each record on the records
# branch keeps fwtest's own and the spec experiments' outputs, and fetching
# a record's files wholesale brings their blobs in (it happened once, in
# M1; docs/EXPOSURE.md). So under every branch, remote branch included, a
# file under a folder named spec-experiments/ or as a spec-side folder, at
# any depth, must be missing too.
# Trees are in a blob-less clone, so this reads no file.
have=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" for-each-ref --format='%(objectname)' refs/heads refs/remotes \
    | sort -u | while read -r c; do GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r "$c"; done \
    | awk -F '\t' -v re="$SPEC_RE" '{ split($1, m, " ") } m[2] == "blob" && $2 ~ re { print m[3] }' \
    | sort -u | GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname)' 2>/dev/null | grep -vc missing || true)
[ "$have" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: $have spec-side output or source file(s) reached through a branch (the records branch?) are in .git"; fail=1; }
if [ $fail -ne 0 ]; then echo "Tell the owner before doing anything else." >&2; exit 1; fi
echo "clean folder at $(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD); no spec-side files on disk or in .git"
  arp/arpeggiator
  arp/budgets
  arp/clock-out-quiet
  m1/wrapup
  m2/budgets
  m2/firmware
  m2/perf-method
  m2/sr3
  m2/staged-nofetch
  m2/start
  m2/wrapup
  m3/budgets
  m3/firmware
  m3/folder-list
  m3/perf-first
  m3/perf-image
  m3/start
  m3/wrapup
  m4/budgets
  m4/firmware
  m4/spi-tidy
  m4/start

  m4b/budgets
  m4b/perf-loaded
  m4b/plaits-demo
  m4b/rule-ids

+# Phase A1: our firmware as a standard `.fwsc` package
+A note from the spec side (session spec-a1-fwsc, 2026-10-27) to the
+firmware side, in the manner of a spec request's answer: what to build,
+from which facts, and how it is tested. Nothing here is built on the
+firmware side yet. Its facts are docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md HW-87 to HW-93
+(section 21); this note adds none of its own and gives no code.
+## The goal
+The firmware side builds our firmware into an update package (`.fwsc`)
+in JieLi's standard format that loads, the same way a stock package does,
+in three places:
+1. the F-Emulator app's package path (it opens `.fwsc` files as the
+   imported type `io.github.japes98.fwsc`, docs/M9-PLAN.md section 1);
+2. fwtest, through its package path (`--package`, docs/HARNESS.md
+   "Packages", from fwtest 0.8.0);
+3. the upstream fm1-emu web build, which boots every firmware from its
+   package.
+The `.fm1img` stays our release format; the `.fwsc` is for compatibility
+with tools that take packages (docs/M9-PLAN.md section 1). A1 does not
+make a package for real hardware: what the chip's loaders and updater
+check is open (Q-26), and M10 decides the boot area and the packaging
+tool. A package that passes all three paths may still be refused by a
+unit; nobody installs one on a unit in A1.
+## Note A1-1 (to the firmware side): a packager in `tools/`
+- Status: open (for the firmware side).
+- What to build, from HW-87 to HW-91 only:
+  - **A second link of the firmware**, for the package, at the address a
+    package's app runs from: the window's start plus the app's offset in
+    the app area, `0x02000120` with the SDK's `0x120`-byte directory
+    (HW-91). The raw image (`app.bin`, linked at `0x02000000`) stays as
+    it is, for fwtest's raw path, the `.fm1img` and the app's raw loader.
+    The two are the same code linked twice; nothing in the firmware may
+    depend on which.
+  - **A packager**, `tools/` (say `tools/fwsc.py`), that makes
+    `small-beeps-<version>.fwsc` from that link's binary: the package
+    header in 20 blocks with our identity in the markers (HW-88: ASCII,
+    at most 19 characters, not another board's prefix); one entry, the
+    flash image (type 0); the flash image (HW-89): the flash header, a
+    directory with the configuration head and the app area's head, a key
+    block of our own with its CRC-16; the app area at flash `0x4000`
+    (HW-90): its head, its directory with `app.bin` (attribute `0x82`)
+    at offset `0x120`, the app, scrambled with the key the key block
+    gives. Every CRC by HW-87's rule: header, flash header, each head and
+    each head's data. Fields the facts don't define (Q-25) are written as
+    0 and listed in the packager's own documentation as unknown.
+  - **What it leaves alone.** The flash image ends at the app area's end,
+    so a package writes nothing past it: not the store's region, not the
+    stock user-patch region (answer 5 in M9-PLAN.md).
+  - **No loader binaries.** None of the three paths runs one (HW-93); the
+    boot area holds only the flash header, the directory and the key
+    block ("Loaders", below).
+  - **Reproducible** (R-REPRO): the same tag gives a byte-identical
+    `.fwsc`, built in the pinned container by the release tooling beside
+    the `.fm1img`.
+  - **A reference reader** in `tools/` that runs HW-93's checks in its
+    order and prints which one fails, so the tests, the app's author and
+    fwtest agree on them.
+- Why: Phase A1 (the owner's prompt, docs/prompts/spec-a1-fwsc.md);
+  answers M9-PLAN.md's question 4 for the emulated paths (our own packer).
+- Logged as: the facts reach the firmware side through HARDWARE-SPEC.md
+  only; the firmware side's PROVENANCE entry names HW-87 to HW-93.
+## How it is tested: the three load paths
+1. **fwtest** (automatic, in CI). With fwtest 0.8.0 pinned: the firmware
+   suite runs a case from the package (`tools/fwtest run
+   small-beeps-<version>.fwsc --package ...`) beside the same case from
+   the raw image; both must show the firmware's normal start (its first
+   screen, its own start-up marks) and the same outputs where the entry
+   address can't matter. `result.json`'s `run.package` must name our
+   identity, the app area `0x04000` and the entry `0x02000120`. The
+   reference reader runs on the package. Unit tests of the packager make
+   a package with each check of HW-93 broken in turn and show fwtest and
+   the reader refuse each, naming the check.
+2. **The F-Emulator app** (by hand, the owner): open the `.fwsc` from
+   Files; the firmware starts as it does from the `.fm1img` of the same
+   tag. The owner records the result in the release notes. (The app's
+   package path is taken to be upstream's unchanged; docs/EMULATOR-PARITY.md,
+   "Packages", asks the owner to confirm.)
+3. **The upstream web build** (by hand, the owner, or a spec-side
+   session; not the firmware side): open the `.fwsc` with the hosted
+   page's "Open .fwsc…" button; the firmware starts. The page's own
+   catalog fetches and runs other firmwares from other sites, some of
+   them on CONTRIBUTING.md's list of material the firmware side never
+   opens or fetches, so a clean session doesn't use the page at all.
+A1 is done when all three boot the same tag's package and the CI case
+passes.
+## Loaders
+- **What a package needs.** None of the three load paths runs the mask
+  ROM, the second-stage loader or the update loader (HW-92, HW-93): they
+  need no loader file at all, so A1's package carries none.
+- **For a hardware package (M10, not A1)**: the SDK's own second-stage
+  loader `uboot.boot` and update loader `ota.bin` (`cpu/wl82/tools/` at

+  release package may carry them, with the SDK's licence text and a
+  `NOTICE` entry, as named binaries checked by SHA-256 that nobody opens.
+  Whether a stock unit accepts them is unknown (M9-PLAN.md section 2;
+- **Not used:** FM1 Open's boot and update files (M-VAVE's, Apache-2.0):
+  on hold, since the owner's A1 prompt keeps every M-VAVE binary out of
+  the repository; M-VAVE's stock package and anything from it: never.
+- The SDK's packaging programs are Windows binaries; A1 doesn't need

+2. The firmware side pins fwtest 0.7.0 (its pull request, as the owner

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

## What is checked

`tools/check-transcripts.py` (C-TRANSCRIPTS in every test record):

- every transcript must be in the folder of its role (a file outside
  `clean/` and `spec/` fails). When `spec/` isn't on disk (a clean folder),

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

## What is checked

`tools/check-transcripts.py` (C-TRANSCRIPTS in every test record):

- every transcript must be in the folder of its role (a file outside
  `clean/` and `spec/` fails). When `spec/` isn't on disk (a clean folder),
  spec transcripts are skipped, not read, and the output says so;
- every transcript must show the SessionStart banner from
  `tools/session-banner.sh` with `status: OK`. Any `CONFIG MISMATCH` fails.

- Needed by: M9 (the app's emulator), USB MIDI (not planned)

## 21. The update package (`.fwsc`) and the loader chain (Phase A1)

What a JieLi update package for the FM-1 is, byte by byte, as far as the
allowed sources give it, and what each step that loads one checks: the
emulator's package path (which the upstream web build and fwtest's
`--package` share, and the F-Emulator app is taken to; HW-93) and the chip's own chain
(HW-92). Written by session spec-a1-fwsc for a packager of our own
(docs/A1-PLAN.md). No stock package was opened for it; what only a stock
file could show is left open (Q-25, Q-26). HW-91 corrects HW-81's
window address. Offsets are in bytes from the start of the structure
named; all multi-byte fields are little-endian.

### HW-87: JieLi's CRC-16 and the header mask
- Fact: Two rules recur in the package:
  - **CRC-16** ("JieLi's CRC-16" below): polynomial `0x1021`, initial
    value 0, bits taken most significant first, no reflection, no final
    XOR (the CRC-16/XMODEM parameters). Check value: the ASCII bytes
    `123456789` give `0x31C3`. A structure's own CRC sits in its first
    two bytes and covers the rest of it, from byte 2 to its end.
  - **The mask** with a 16-bit seed: keep a 16-bit value `k`, starting at
    the seed; XOR each byte, in order, with `k`'s low 8 bits; after each
    byte, shift `k` left by one, keeping 16 bits, and if `k`'s top bit was
    1 before the shift, XOR it with `0x1021`. The mask is its own inverse.
    The first four mask bytes from seed `0xFFFF` are `FF DF 9F 1F`. The
    "header key `0xFFFF`" below is this mask with seed `0xFFFF`.
  M9-PLAN.md called the CRC CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (initial value `0xFFFF`),
  after RE; that is wrong for these structures: the SDK's own packer and
  the emulator's package path start from 0.
- Sources: SDK `cpu/wl82/tools/packufw/source/JLpack.cpp` lines 23-44
  (the CRC: table of `0x1021` multiples, initial 0) and 181, 198 (a
  head's CRC over the head after its first two bytes, stored first); RE
  `docs/io/11-ota-protocol.md`, "The .fwsc logical image" (the header key
  `0xFFFF`) and "Known open items" (`jl_crc16` named CCITT-FALSE); the
  emulator's package path (HW-93: the mask, and CRCs from 0 that pass on
  the stock packages it boots).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK for the CRC; the mask emulator-only, its seed
  RE)
- Needed by: A1

### HW-88: The package file: header blocks, header, entries
- Fact: A package is a header in blocks, then data:
  - **Blocks.** The file's first 960 bytes are 20 blocks of 48 (`0x30`)
    bytes. In each block the first 47 (`0x2F`) bytes are header data and
    the last is a marker. The 20 data parts, in order, make the **logical
    header** (940 bytes). Everything from file offset 960 on is data,
    plain. The **logical image** is the logical header followed by the
    file from offset 960: logical offset `n` is file offset `n + 20` for
    `n` ≥ 940.
  - **Markers.** Block `i`'s marker (file offset `48·i + 47`) is the
    package's identity's character `i` plus `i + 1` (modulo 256) while
    the identity lasts, and `0x7D` after it; the stock FM-1 package's
    identity is its name (`FM-1_0nn`, 8 characters, so blocks 8 to 19
    carry `0x7D`). The emulator reads the identity back from the markers;
    one that starts with `SMK`, `MKE` or `STARRYKEY` (any case) makes it
    boot the SMK-37 keyboard instead of the FM-1, and if the data byte at
    file offset 1007 (where a 21st block's marker would be) is `0x7D` it
    first tries a longer header, then falls back to 20 blocks. So an FM-1
    package's identity is ASCII, at most 19 characters (ending the
    markers with `0x7D`, as stock does), and starts with none of those.
  - **Header.** The logical header's first 64 (`0x40`) bytes are masked
    with the header key (HW-87). Unmasked: bytes 0-1 the header's
    CRC-16 over bytes 2-63; bytes 8-9 the entry count. RE names the
    header's fields, in order, header CRC, list CRC, image size and entry
    count; where the list CRC and the image size sit, and what they
    cover, is not given (Q-25).
  - **Entries.** Entry `k` is the 80 (`0x50`) bytes at logical offset
    `64 + 80·k`, masked on its own with the header key. Unmasked: bytes
    0-1 its type, type 0 being the **flash image**; bytes 8-11 its data's
    logical offset; bytes 12-15 its data's length. Its name, its CRC and
    its other fields are not given (Q-25). The stock package has eight
    entries, the flash image (`flash.bin`), `info.log`, `USR`, the
    loader's configuration (`isd_config.ini`), the update loader
    (`ota.bin`), `script.ver`, `blimit.bin` and `tail.bin`; the SDK's
    packaging adds the update loader as type 100 and `script.ver` (the
    packaging tool's version, `AC791N-v0.01-cfg_tool-v0.10` in the SDK)
    to the package before turning it into the update file.
  The emulator's package path reads only the header's CRC, the entry
  count and the first type-0 entry; a package for it needs no other
  entry. What the chip's updater needs is Q-26.
- Sources: RE `docs/io/11-ota-protocol.md`, "The .fwsc logical image"
  (the 20 blocks, 47 + 1 bytes, the logical image, the header's fields,
  the eight entries); RE `docs/architecture.md` §2 (a UFW package for the
  chip "AC791N"); SDK `cpu/wl82/tools/download.c` lines 258-264 (the
  update loader added with `-type 100`, then `script.ver`, then the
  conversion to the update file) and `cpu/wl82/tools/script.ver`; the
  emulator's package path (the markers, the identity, the field offsets
  read, the board chosen by the identity).
- Standing: confirmed (RE) for the blocks and the logical image; the
  markers, the entry's field offsets and the header's emulator-only
- Needed by: A1

### HW-89: The flash image: its header and directory
- Fact: The flash image (the type-0 entry's data) is written to the
  flash chip from offset 0 (the stock one covers `0x00000`-`0x93FFF`,
  HW-80). It starts with 32-byte heads, each masked on its own with the
  header key (HW-87):
  - **The flash header**, the head at offset 0: unmasked, bytes 0-1 its
    CRC-16 over bytes 2-31; 2-3 a size for the programmer
    (`size4burner`); 4-7 the VID (4 bytes); 8-11 the flash size; 12 the
    file system's version; 13 an alignment, in units of 256 bytes; 14
    reserved; 15 a special-options byte; 16-31 the PID (16 bytes). The
    emulator's package path copies it, unmasked, into the boot block
    (HW-91) and checks nothing in it.
  - **Directory heads**, from offset 32, one after another, until the
    first with a non-zero "last" field. Unmasked, each is: bytes 0-1 its
    CRC-16 over bytes 2-31; 2-3 its data's CRC-16; 4-7 its data's flash
    offset; 8-11 its data's length; 12 its attribute; 13 reserved; 14-15
    "last" (non-zero on the directory's last head); 16-31 its name, ASCII,
    padded with zero bytes.
  Two heads are required, found by name (the first match wins):
  - `isd_config.ini`, the loader's configuration: at its data's offset,
    32 bytes (the **key block**, HW-90) and right after them their
    CRC-16 (2 bytes). These are stored as they are, not masked.
  - `app_dir_head` with attribute `0x81`: its offset is the start of the
    **app area** (HW-90). FM-1-RE calls the app area's table
    `app_area_head`; the name the readers match is `app_dir_head`.
  The stock directory also has the second-stage loader `uboot.boot` at
  flash offset `0xA0` (which the mask ROM loads, HW-92) and the loader's
  configuration at `0x38D0` (HW-80). The emulator's package path checks
  no head's CRC or its data's CRC; whether the chip's loader does is Q-26.
  A packager fills them by the rule above.

### HW-90: The app area: the chip key and its scrambling
- Fact: The app area starts at the `app_dir_head` head's offset `A`
  (`0x4000` on the FM-1; HW-91 says why it must be). It is scrambled
  with a 16-bit **chip key**:
  - **The key from the key block** (the 32 bytes `b[0]`-`b[31]` of
    HW-89): let `s` be the sum of `b[0]`-`b[15]` modulo 256; if `s` ≥
    `0xE0`, take `s` = `0xAA`; else if `s` ≤ `0x10`, take `s` = `0x55`.
    Then bit `i` of the key (`i` = 0 to 15) is 1 when `b[16 + i]` XOR
    `b[15 − i]` is less than `s`, else 0. Any key block gives a key; the
    stock package's gives `0x980F`.
  - **The scrambling.** From `A`, the area is cut into 32-byte chunks;
    the chunk at offset `r` from `A` (`r` = 0, 32, 64, …) is masked
    (HW-87) with the seed `key XOR (r / 4)`, keeping 16 bits; the last
    chunk may be shorter. The first chunk is the **area head**, a 32-byte
    head (HW-89's layout, not masked again) whose length field (bytes
    8-11) is the length of the scrambled area from `A`, the area head
    included. Bytes past that length are left as they are.
  - **The area's directory**, once unscrambled: 32-byte heads from `A +
    32`, each in HW-89's layout but not masked, until the first with a
    non-zero "last" field or the area's end. `app.bin`, with attribute
    `0x82`, is the app: its offset is from `A`, and its length the app's
    length. The stock directory also lists `cfg_tool.bin` and `cfg`

    `USR` (whose offsets are flash offsets). With the area head and eight
    heads the directory is `0x120` bytes, so the stock `app.bin` is at
    `A + 0x120` (flash `0x4120`).

  emulated load paths any key works, as long as the area is scrambled

### HW-87: JieLi's CRC-16 and the header mask
- Fact: Two rules recur in the package:
  - **CRC-16** ("JieLi's CRC-16" below): polynomial `0x1021`, initial
    value 0, bits taken most significant first, no reflection, no final
    XOR (the CRC-16/XMODEM parameters). Check value: the ASCII bytes
    `123456789` give `0x31C3`. A structure's own CRC sits in its first
    two bytes and covers the rest of it, from byte 2 to its end.
  - **The mask** with a 16-bit seed: keep a 16-bit value `k`, starting at
    the seed; XOR each byte, in order, with `k`'s low 8 bits; after each
    byte, shift `k` left by one, keeping 16 bits, and if `k`'s top bit was
    1 before the shift, XOR it with `0x1021`. The mask is its own inverse.
    The first four mask bytes from seed `0xFFFF` are `FF DF 9F 1F`. The
    "header key `0xFFFF`" below is this mask with seed `0xFFFF`.
  M9-PLAN.md called the CRC CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (initial value `0xFFFF`),
  after RE; that is wrong for these structures: the SDK's own packer and
  the emulator's package path start from 0.
- Sources: SDK `cpu/wl82/tools/packufw/source/JLpack.cpp` lines 23-44
  (the CRC: table of `0x1021` multiples, initial 0) and 181, 198 (a
  head's CRC over the head after its first two bytes, stored first); RE
  `docs/io/11-ota-protocol.md`, "The .fwsc logical image" (the header key
  `0xFFFF`) and "Known open items" (`jl_crc16` named CCITT-FALSE); the
  emulator's package path (HW-93: the mask, and CRCs from 0 that pass on
  the stock packages it boots).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK for the CRC; the mask emulator-only, its seed
  RE)
- Needed by: A1

### HW-88: The package file: header blocks, header, entries
- Fact: A package is a header in blocks, then data:
  - **Blocks.** The file's first 960 bytes are 20 blocks of 48 (`0x30`)
    bytes. In each block the first 47 (`0x2F`) bytes are header data and
    the last is a marker. The 20 data parts, in order, make the **logical
    header** (940 bytes). Everything from file offset 960 on is data,
    plain. The **logical image** is the logical header followed by the
    file from offset 960: logical offset `n` is file offset `n + 20` for
    `n` ≥ 940.
  - **Markers.** Block `i`'s marker (file offset `48·i + 47`) is the
    package's identity's character `i` plus `i + 1` (modulo 256) while
    the identity lasts, and `0x7D` after it; the stock FM-1 package's
    identity is its name (`FM-1_0nn`, 8 characters, so blocks 8 to 19
    carry `0x7D`). The emulator reads the identity back from the markers;
    one that starts with `SMK`, `MKE` or `STARRYKEY` (any case) makes it
    boot the SMK-37 keyboard instead of the FM-1, and if the data byte at
    file offset 1007 (where a 21st block's marker would be) is `0x7D` it
    first tries a longer header, then falls back to 20 blocks. So an FM-1
    package's identity is ASCII, at most 19 characters (ending the
    markers with `0x7D`, as stock does), and starts with none of those.
  - **Header.** The logical header's first 64 (`0x40`) bytes are masked
    with the header key (HW-87). Unmasked: bytes 0-1 the header's
    CRC-16 over bytes 2-63; bytes 8-9 the entry count. RE names the
    header's fields, in order, header CRC, list CRC, image size and entry
    count; where the list CRC and the image size sit, and what they
    cover, is not given (Q-25).
  - **Entries.** Entry `k` is the 80 (`0x50`) bytes at logical offset
    `64 + 80·k`, masked on its own with the header key. Unmasked: bytes
    0-1 its type, type 0 being the **flash image**; bytes 8-11 its data's
    logical offset; bytes 12-15 its data's length. Its name, its CRC and
    its other fields are not given (Q-25). The stock package has eight
    entries, the flash image (`flash.bin`), `info.log`, `USR`, the
    loader's configuration (`isd_config.ini`), the update loader
    (`ota.bin`), `script.ver`, `blimit.bin` and `tail.bin`; the SDK's
    packaging adds the update loader as type 100 and `script.ver` (the
    packaging tool's version, `AC791N-v0.01-cfg_tool-v0.10` in the SDK)
    to the package before turning it into the update file.
  The emulator's package path reads only the header's CRC, the entry
  count and the first type-0 entry; a package for it needs no other
  entry. What the chip's updater needs is Q-26.
- Sources: RE `docs/io/11-ota-protocol.md`, "The .fwsc logical image"
  (the 20 blocks, 47 + 1 bytes, the logical image, the header's fields,
  the eight entries); RE `docs/architecture.md` §2 (a UFW package for the
  chip "AC791N"); SDK `cpu/wl82/tools/download.c` lines 258-264 (the
  update loader added with `-type 100`, then `script.ver`, then the
  conversion to the update file) and `cpu/wl82/tools/script.ver`; the
  emulator's package path (the markers, the identity, the field offsets
  read, the board chosen by the identity).
- Standing: confirmed (RE) for the blocks and the logical image; the
  markers, the entry's field offsets and the header's emulator-only
- Needed by: A1

### HW-89: The flash image: its header and directory
- Fact: The flash image (the type-0 entry's data) is written to the
  flash chip from offset 0 (the stock one covers `0x00000`-`0x93FFF`,
  HW-80). It starts with 32-byte heads, each masked on its own with the
  header key (HW-87):
  - **The flash header**, the head at offset 0: unmasked, bytes 0-1 its
    CRC-16 over bytes 2-31; 2-3 a size for the programmer
    (`size4burner`); 4-7 the VID (4 bytes); 8-11 the flash size; 12 the

    reserved; 15 a special-options byte; 16-31 the PID (16 bytes). The
    emulator's package path copies it, unmasked, into the boot block
    (HW-91) and checks nothing in it.
  - **Directory heads**, from offset 32, one after another, until the
    first with a non-zero "last" field. Unmasked, each is: bytes 0-1 its
    CRC-16 over bytes 2-31; 2-3 its data's CRC-16; 4-7 its data's flash
    offset; 8-11 its data's length; 12 its attribute; 13 reserved; 14-15
